title: Prepare an authorized snapshot for a protected time-bounded local handoff

requirements.invariant: A protected export consumes an already-authorized immutable visibility-bound snapshot, creates only a short-lived local artifact lease and returns a typed destination/cleanup receipt; a path, URL, file or provider handle never becomes durable domain state.

Export evidence preserves the exact approved visibility scope and projection/profile version, excludes private paths, expiring bearer URLs and hidden-row facts, and cannot widen authorization during rendering or destination handoff.

Artifact preparation and handoff operate on a completed immutable query snapshot and never recalculate business meaning, infer missing evidence, mutate accounting state or act as another query authority.

Unknown formats, destination intents, scope/profile/authority mismatches, expired leases, illegal lifecycle transitions, changed hashes and malformed canonical evidence fail with stable non-enumerating results and no accepted partial receipt.

The exact target-only implementation commit passes deterministic contract tests, source-contamination and generated-contract checks, clean artifact validation, and both isolated target builds before this shared foundation is called verified.

items: ProtectedArtifactExportID, ProtectedArtifactSnapshotID, ProtectedArtifactVisibilityScopeID, ProtectedArtifactProfileVersion and ProtectedArtifactSHA256 are bounded validated values; content kind, destination intent, destination outcome, lifecycle phase and cleanup disposition are closed enums.

ProtectedArtifactSnapshotReference binds stable snapshot identity, exact immutable snapshot hash, visibility scope, projection/profile version and authority version without carrying entity, Account, Principal, path, URL or provider values.

ProtectedArtifactExportRequest is created only through a policy that constrains format, destination intent, positive output ceiling, lease duration and canonical evidence size, and derives one request fingerprint.

ProtectedArtifactLifecycle validates a monotonic requested/materialized/handoff-recorded/cleanup-required/cleaned or terminal failure/cancellation transition path using exact request/snapshot/output identity.

ProtectedArtifactExportReceipt binds request fingerprint, snapshot/profile/authority scope, output byte count/hash, lease expiry, destination outcome and cleanup disposition while explicitly remaining evidence-only and not proof of filesystem protection/deletion or client delivery authorization.

postgresSchema.notApplicable: This provider-free local evidence contract creates no Postgres relation, view, function, check, uniqueness rule or index.

serverHandlers.notApplicable: No rendering, share, print, download, upload, delivery, cleanup, business command or trusted server handler executes.

dataApiGrants.notApplicable: No Data API schema, relation, view or function is exposed.

rlsPolicies.notApplicable: The contract accepts only a caller-supplied already-authorized snapshot reference and creates no server row; snapshot authorization remains with the owning query/RLS slice.

syncStreams.notApplicable: Generated artifacts and lifecycle evidence are not synchronized domain authority; no PowerSync Stream or local synchronized table is defined.

items: Request, lifecycle and receipt encode to deterministic sorted canonical bytes and reconstruct through the same validators without network, filesystem, keychain, provider SDK or mutable process state.
Expiry, cancellation, failure, destination outcome and cleanup-required state survive restart; illegal or reordered transitions and changed request/snapshot/output identity fail atomically.
Canonical evidence excludes raw paths, URLs, credentials, provider handles and human/account/entity identifiers and stays under a fixed size ceiling.

storageMedia.notApplicable: This slice stores no bytes and performs no file or Storage I/O. A future platform adapter must prove data-protection attributes and physical cleanup separately; O-023 still governs attachment retention/deletion.

appMcp.notApplicable: No app, MCP, renderer, share sheet, print controller, file picker or download adapter is wired. Product report/export snapshots and O-036 client-delivery eligibility remain separate owning slices.

migrationReconciliation.notApplicable: No Firebase artifact/path/URL is imported and no migration runs. Later adapters regenerate target artifacts from authorized immutable snapshots.

items: Stable diagnostic codes distinguish invalid bounded values, scope/profile/authority mismatch, disallowed content/destination, invalid lease bounds, duplicate/illegal transitions, request/output/hash mismatch, expiry, canonical tamper and evidence-size overflow.
Receipts expose only safe lifecycle categories and hashes. They do not assert physical deletion, destination delivery to a client, retained artifact bytes or feature/cutover authority.

The contracts are additive target-only Swift code/tests, import no provider SDK, alter no source application or current report/export implementation, contact no hosted service and can be reverted without external state change.
O-023 attachment retention and O-036 report-content/client-delivery decisions remain explicit later gates; this slice cannot satisfy or bypass them.

verification.expected: Closed values, exact already-authorized snapshot scope, policy-bounded request, request fingerprint, legal lifecycle and evidence-only receipt validate deterministically without recalculation or provider values.

Equivalent request/lifecycle/receipt evidence normalizes to identical bytes and hashes, decodes and revalidates offline, and preserves expiry, destination outcome and cleanup-required state across restart.

Unsafe values, scope/profile/authority/request/output mismatches, disallowed formats/intents, invalid bounds, expiry, illegal/reordered transitions, changed hashes, noncanonical bytes and oversized evidence fail with stable codes and no partial accepted receipt.

verification.owner: pull-request CI Isolated target environment job
verification.expected: The exact implementation commit passes conversion traceability, source-contamination and generated-contract checks, all target tests, macOS and generic iOS Simulator target builds, and clean tracked-diff validation.

notes: Decision-independent target technical-control foundation. It stops before snapshot preparation, report/export semantics, O-036 client-delivery policy, O-023 attachment retention, filesystem/data-protection APIs, renderer bytes, destination adapters, app/MCP wiring, hosted resources, migration, production release or cutover.
